text.p: Investors with intermediate investment horizons should hold shares of Poland's Bank Gdanski SA, the brokerage unit of Bank Handlowy SA said in a report.
The report dated February 7 and released to the press on Monday said the bank was increasing banking activity profits but had a relatively low share of credits in total assets.

"At the end of the first half of 1996 receivables from clients and the budget sector accounted for about 28.5 percent of total assets. In the group of full service banks this share was 36 percent," the report said.
But Gdanski has a relatively high share of deposits in total assets, Handlowy said.
It said if BIG, which last month rose its Gdanski stake by 31.9 percent to 63.4 percent, changed the full-service character of Gdanski, the bank could suffer.

Handlowy said Gdanski should lift net profit to 111.8 million zlotys this year from 101.2 million last year. It said net interest revenue would increase to 377.3 million zlotys from 307.1 million zlotys in 1996.
Handlowy said the bank's price-earnings ratio, which was at 10.9 at the time of the report when Gdanski shares cost 43 zlotys, should fall to 7.5 at the end of this year.
Gdanski closed on the Warsaw bourse at 47 zlotys on Friday.
